## Construction

Let $\zeta(a)=\sum_{d\ge 1} d^{-a}$, which converges because $a>1$. Set
$$C = 1 + 2\zeta(a).$$
Define the sequence recursively. Let $x_0 = 0$. For $n\ge 1$, having chosen $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$ in $[0,C]$, choose $x_n\in[0,C]$ such that
$$|x_n - x_j| \ge |n-j|^{-a} \qquad \text{for all } j<n. \tag{$*$}$$

**Why such an $x_n$ exists.** Condition $(*)$ forbids $x_n$ from lying in the open interval $I_j=\big(x_j-(n-j)^{-a},\,x_j+(n-j)^{-a}\big)$ for each $j<n$. The interval $I_j$ has length $2(n-j)^{-a}$, so the forbidden intervals have total length at most
$$\sum_{j<n} 2(n-j)^{-a} = 2\sum_{d=1}^{n} d^{-a} \le 2\zeta(a) < C.$$
Hence $[0,C]$ minus these intervals has positive measure and is nonempty. So $x_n$ can be chosen.

**Verification.** The sequence is bounded by construction, since $|x_n|\le C$ for all $n$. For distinct $i,j$, say $j<i$, condition $(*)$ applied when $x_i$ was chosen gives $|x_i-x_j|\ge |i-j|^{-a}$. Therefore
$$|x_i-x_j|\,|i-j|^{a}\ge 1$$
for every pair of distinct nonnegative integers $i,j$.

ANSWER: Let $C=1+2\zeta(a)$ with $\zeta(a)=\sum_{d\ge1}d^{-a}$. Take $x_0=0$ and, for $n\ge1$, let $x_n\in[0,C]$ be any point with $|x_n-x_j|\ge |n-j|^{-a}$ for all $j<n$. Such a point exists because the forbidden open intervals have total length at most $2\zeta(a)<C$. The sequence satisfies $|x_i|\le C$ and $|x_i-x_j|\,|i-j|^a\ge1$.
